subject: Mathematics

source.subtopic: Use calendars to calculate and describe length of time in days or weeks (weeks 1-4)

show.line: This is a calendar. Seven days make a week. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday!

rounds.prompt: Count the days in one row of the calendar. How many days in a week?
Today is the 3rd. Lebo's party is on the 10th. How many days until the party?
rounds.praise: Yes! Seven days, one whole week.

rounds.prompt: Two weeks. How many days is that? Say the number.
Find the 15th on the calendar. Which day of the week is it?

rounds.story: Holidays start on Friday the 20th and end on Sunday the 29th. Is that more or less than a week?
rounds.praise: More! Nine days is more than seven.

hints: One row on the calendar is one week, seven days.
Count the squares from one date to the other.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! Today is Monday the 1st. I will find one week later.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: One week later is Monday the 5th!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! A week is seven days. Monday the 1st plus seven is Monday the 8th.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's count seven days together. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Monday the 8th!

parent_line: Can read a calendar and count days and weeks between dates.
